---
title: "Connect lab services"
description: "Put biology databases, notebooks and other MCP connectors behind the gateway, so every call is checked, approved and recorded."
---

Agents in labs use more than instruments. They search the literature, look up
compounds and targets, read and write protocols, and could place orders. Many of
these services are offered as MCP servers, often called connectors. Inspect Labs puts
a connector behind the same gateway as a Lab, so its calls are checked, approved if
needed, journaled and recorded like any other lab action.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Treat results as outside data
What a connector returns can be wrong, and it can contain text written to mislead
the agent. The lab log records a digest of every result and its first part, so
reviewers can see what the agent was shown.
:::

## Review a connector once

Snapshot the connector's tools into a profile, starting from a built-in template:

```bash
inspect-labs connector snapshot pubmed \
  --url https://pubmed.mcp.claude.com/mcp --template pubmed \
  --output connectors/pubmed.json
```

The profile pins each tool's description and input schema by digest and gives each
an action type. Review it before use:

- **Tools without an action type are never offered to the agent.** The snapshot
  lists them as `unclassified`; give each one a type to offer it.
- **A changed tool is refused.** Before every call, on the same connection as the
  call, the tool's definition is checked against the profile. If the server changed
  its description or schema, the call is refused until you snapshot and review it
  again. A
  connector can't quietly turn a search into a write.
- **Sequences are screened before they leave.** List the arguments that carry DNA or
  protein sequences in `sequence_arguments`. A call carrying a sequence runs only if
  a configured screen says every sequence is clear; flagged, unknown or unscreened
  sequences are refused.
- **Server hints are shown, never trusted.** A server can label its own tools as
  read-only or destructive. The profile keeps those labels for reviewers, and the
  snapshot lists any tool classified as a read that its server says writes. The
  gateway decides by your classification alone, since a server's labels are its own
  claims.
- **Credentials stay out of profiles.** `env` names environment variables to pass to
  a local server; their values are read when it starts.

## Serve or evaluate

```bash
inspect-labs serve --connector connectors/pubmed.json --lab-log .research/pubmed-session.json
```

In an evaluation, use `ConnectorLab(profile, directory)` as the Lab in
`connect_lab`. The default rules apply as for any Lab: reads run, while irreversible
and external calls need a person's approval.

## Built-in templates

Templates are reviewed starting points; a snapshot applies them only to tools with
matching names and leaves the rest unclassified.

| Template | Service | Classified as | Sign-in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pubmed` | PubMed (Anthropic-hosted) | All read | None |
| `chembl` | ChEMBL | All read | None |
| `biorxiv` | bioRxiv preprints | All read | None |
| `clinical-trials` | ClinicalTrials.gov | All read | None |
| `open-targets` | Open Targets | All read | None |
| `protocols-io` | protocols.io | Reads; edits reversible; replacing or deleting steps irreversible | Token |
| `10x-genomics` | 10x Genomics Cloud | Uploads external; starting analyses irreversible | Token |
| `synapse` | Synapse | Proxy tools hide the real tool, so every call is held | Sign-in |
| `benchling` | Benchling | Notebook edits and its delegating agent tool irreversible; names unconfirmed | Sign-in |
| `biorender` | BioRender | Figure creation reversible; names unconfirmed | Sign-in |

## Checked against Claude's life-sciences connectors

On 4 October 2026 the templates were compared with the connectors in Anthropic's
[life-sciences plugins](https://github.com/anthropics/life-sciences) and with each
server's live tool list. The comparison listed tools only; no tool was called.

- **PubMed, bioRxiv, ChEMBL, ClinicalTrials and Open Targets** answered without
  sign-in. Their live tools match the templates exactly, and each server's own
  read-only labels agree with the templates.
- **bioRxiv, ChEMBL and ClinicalTrials** are listed in the plugins at
  `mcp.deepsense.ai`, which refused anonymous requests. The templates use the
  Anthropic-hosted addresses at `hcls.mcp.claude.com`, which answered.
- **BioRender, Synapse, Consensus, AdisInsight, Cortellis, Medidata, Owkin and Wiley
  Scholar Gateway** need an OAuth sign-in, which Inspect Labs connectors don't
  support yet. Their tools couldn't be listed; only BioRender and Synapse have
  templates, built from directory listings and source code.
- **10x Genomics and ToolUniverse** ship as desktop extension bundles that run
  locally. No DNA
synthesis provider offers an MCP connector yet; an ordering tool should be
classified `external`, with its sequence arguments screened.
